summary: Regression verification after deployment-readiness fixes (Redis removed → in-memory sliding-window limiter, blockchain/web3 removed, Google SSO uses window.location.origin, static Expo export rebuilt). ALL requested checks PASS with no regressions. Backend health, both logins (free + admin), rate limiting on /api/auth/password/reset (5 non-429 → 6th/7th 429 with Retry-After: 300), rate-limit headers on normal endpoints, personal-assistant models endpoint (3 models), Claude Haiku 4.5 real response, clean backend logs (no redis/web3 import errors), token-revocation pytest 3/3 PASS. Frontend: login page renders with Google SSO button, free-user login works, /features/travel-visa loads onboarding dashboard, /features/ai-writer AI Chat tab exposes ai-chat-model-picker with all 3 model options. Pre-existing test-suite drift in tests/test_session_persistence_p0p1p2.py (expects Bearer session_token in login body, backend uses cookie session) is NOT caused by the limiter rewrite.

Middleware enforcement confirmed BEFORE the router.

backend_verification.backend_logs_clean: PASS — tail -n 400 /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log and backend.out.log filtered for /redis|web3|polygon|importerror|modulenotfound/i → 0 matches. No import errors after Redis/web3 removal.
backend_verification.pytest_session_persistence: MIXED (PRE-EXISTING, NOT LIMITER-RELATED) — tests/test_session_persistence_p0p1p2.py: 6 passed / 5 failed / 4 errors. All failures are due to the test file expecting `session_token` in the JSON login response body and Bearer-token auth for /api/auth/me, while the current backend uses cookie-based session auth (login response has no session_token). The one limiter-adjacent test (TestRateLimiterConfiguration::test_auth_me_rate_limit_header) fails because it depends on Bearer token being present in login body — but the limiter header IS correctly 240 on /api/auth/me, verified via direct curl. This is test-suite drift, not a limiter rewrite regression.

action_items: NONE for deployment fixes — no regressions. Optional (pre-existing, out of scope): tests/test_session_persistence_p0p1p2.py should be updated to use cookie-based auth (Set-Cookie: session_id) instead of expecting session_token in JSON body + Bearer header. 5 failures + 4 errors traceable to this drift; the limiter enforcement itself is verified working correctly via curl and via the token-revocation pytest which does pass 3/3.
critical_code_review_comments: utils/api_rate_limiter.py — in-memory SlidingWindowCounter behaves correctly: budget of 5/300s on /api/auth/password/reset enforced from same IP without any bypass header, 429 emits Retry-After: 300. X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining headers correctly attached to non-429 responses on normal endpoints (240 on /auth/me, 300 on /personal-assistant/models).

The password/reset route itself returns 404 (route not registered in the router tree), but middleware still applies rate limiting before routing — desired defense-in-depth behavior. If the intent is for that endpoint to exist, main agent should verify why POST /api/auth/password/reset is unregistered (may be intentional if password reset flow is via a different path).

personal_assistant.py send-message endpoint uses request body field name `content` (not `message`). If any client is sending `message`, they will get 422 'Field required'. Not caused by this iteration.

success_rate.backend: 100% for the deployment-fix scope (health, both logins, rate-limit enforcement + headers, AI models regression, clean logs, 3/3 token-revocation pytest). Session-persistence pytest 6/15 pass — but 100% of its failures are pre-existing cookie-vs-Bearer test drift, not caused by the limiter rewrite.
success_rate.frontend: 100% for the requested sanity checks (login page + Google SSO visible, free-user login, travel-visa dashboard, ai-writer AI Chat model picker with 3 options).
